title: Asynchronous Performance Radar and Calibration Playbook
author: Aisha Mendoza
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines Redwood's Asynchronous Performance Radar: a lightweight, calendar-driven approach to continuous performance signals, manager calibration, and integration checkpoints that span hiring through the first year. The goal is to reduce synchronous meeting load, speed decisioning, and embed objective signal collection into the existing hiring/onboarding lifecycle.

Intended audience:
- People Ops partners
- Engineering managers and people managers
- ICs preparing self-assessments
- Hiring managers and interview panel leads

Goals and success criteria:
- Provide a reliable, repeatable quarterly "radar" that aggregates: hiring fit signals, onboarding progress, 1:1 feedback extracts, and objective contribution metrics.
- Reduce time-to-decision for promotion/role changes by 25% compared to a purely synchronous calibration cycle.
- Maintain calibration coverage across 100% of managers each quarter.
- Surface candidates and new hires with risks within the first 90 days for proactive intervention.

Scope and exclusions:
- Scope: Full-time employees and contractors in technical and product functions during hire -> first 12 months -> ongoing quarterly cadence. Applies to distributed and remote-work locations.
- Exclusions: Executive promotion committees (follow executive promotion process) and localized legal/performance-withdrawal processes (those follow HR casework templates).

Key concepts:
- Radar window: A 2-week asynchronous collection period at the end of each quarter where managers and stakeholders submit standardized signals.
- Signal types: Quantitative (OKR progress, ticket throughput, latency of code reviews) and Qualitative (peer praise, feedback snippets, interview calibration notes).
- Calibration packet: A per-manager aggregated summary used by People Ops to run lightweight cross-team calibration.

Process overview (high level):
1) Pre-window (Q-1 week): People Ops publishes the radar packet template and runs a freshness check on onboarding checklists and hiring artifacts.
2) Window open (Day 0 — 2 weeks): Managers submit radar packets for each direct report. Hiring managers must attach interview feedback summary for hires in the last 120 days. ICs may optionally submit self-notes (recommended for promotion candidates).
3) Aggregation (Day 15—17): People Ops validates packets for completeness and computes derived metrics for reportbacks.
4) Calibration (Day 18—21): Asynchronous calibration comments collected in the packet; People Ops publishes a short highlights digest and a list of action items.
5) Close and follow-up (Day 22—30): Managers execute identified actions (career conversations, onboarding plans, PIP triggers) and update the ticket. People Ops tracks closure.

Detailed responsibilities:
- People Ops:
  - Publish radar window calendar at least one quarter in advance.
  - Maintain the packet template and scoring rubric.
  - Run completeness checks and surface outliers.
  - Facilitate escalation to HR for potential formal performance issues.
- Manager:
  - Complete one radar packet per direct report during the window. Attach required artifacts for new hires (interview feedback, onboarding checklist status, first-30/60/90 comments).
  - Provide at least two concrete examples (bullet points) each for strengths and areas to watch.
  - Schedule follow-up discussions within 10 business days when action is required.
- IC/Individual contributor:
  - Optional self-notes (recommended when seeking promotion).
  - Keep role-specific metrics updated in the team dashboard to feed quantitative signals.
- Hiring manager / Interview panel leads:
  - Attach the interview calibration memo for hires within first 120 days. Call out any post-hire concerns (knowledge gaps, ramp delays).

Packet template (fields to be completed):
- Employee name
- Role and manager
- Hire date (if under 12 months)
- Onboarding status (Complete / Partial / Behind) with checklist link
- Core contribution highlights (3 bullets)
- Strengths (2 bullets)
- Areas to watch (2 bullets)
- Example evidence (links to PRs, tickets, meeting notes)
- Quantitative metrics (list metrics & values; e.g., OKR progress 60%, code review mean latency 1.2 days)
- Interview calibration note (if <120 days since hire)
- Recommended action (None / Coaching / Development Plan / Formal HR Process)
- Manager confidence level (High / Medium / Low) 

Scoring rubric (text table):
- Overall banding: Exceeds / Meets / Partially Meets / Below
- Signals and weight:
  - Objective contribution metrics: 40%
  - Peer and cross-team feedback: 25%
  - Manager assessment and examples: 25%
  - Interview/onboarding fit signals: 10%

Example rubric interpretation:
- Exceeds: Objective metrics above target AND corroborating peer feedback OR multiple high-impact deliverables in the window.
- Meets: Mostly on-target metrics, reliable fulfillment of role responsibilities.
- Partially Meets: Several missing metrics or one sustained area of concern; recommended short coaching plan.
- Below: Repeated missed commitments, multiple negative peer signals — escalate to formal HR casework.

Hiring + onboarding touchpoints integrated into radar:
- Interview phase: Panel lead completes "post-hire calibration memo" 1 week after start if candidate accepted. Memo includes interview contradictions, onboarding risk flags, and recommended early learning plan.
- Day 7 checkpoint: Hiring manager posts a 7-day first impressions note in the packet (highly recommended).
- Day 30/60/90: Standard onboarding checklist items mapped to radar packet fields (status and blockers must be present if not complete).

Asynchronous calibration guidance (how to contribute comments):
- All comments should be evidence-linked and <300 words. Provide clear examples: dates, PR numbers, or links.
- When disagreeing with a manager assessment, mark as peer-comment and include the alternative signal. People Ops will mediate where disagreement exceeds two commenters.
- Use tags in the packet for speed: #onboarding-risk #promotion-candidate #needs-coaching

Manager checklists (quick):
- Before window opens: Sync team dashboards and ensure metrics are updated.
- During window: For each direct report, fill packet, attach artifacts, mark recommended action.
- After window: Schedule follow-up conversations and update People Ops ticket with completion notes.

Escalations and exceptions:
- Formal HR escalation should be initiated if a packet maps to "Below" band or if manager confidence is Low with corroborating negative signals.
- For urgent issues surfaced between windows (safety, legal, or severe misconduct), use the immediate HR incident channel — do not wait for the radar window.
- For role transitions requested out-of-cycle (rapid promotion or demotion), submit a fast-track packet with supporting artifacts; People Ops will triage within 5 business days.

Data & reporting:
- People Ops produces a quarterly calibration digest containing: number of packets, band distribution, number of promotion recommendations, onboarding-risk list, time-to-resolution for action items.
- Dashboards: Team leads must maintain one canonical team dashboard that exports metrics to the People Ops data pipeline (fields: employee_id, role, manager, OKR_percent_complete, onboarding_percent).

Sample timeline (example quarter):
- Week -12: Calendar published for next four quarters.
- Week -1: People Ops sanity-check and template refresh.
- Window Day 0—14: Manager submissions open.
- Day 15—17: People Ops aggregation and outlier detection.
- Day 18—21: Asynchronous calibration comments.
- Day 22—30: Action item execution and closeout.

Templates (appendix):
- 7-day first impressions note (example):
  - Role: Senior Backend Engineer
  - Positive: Shipped infra test harness (PR #2341) within first week; proactively paired on onboarding docs.
  - Risk: Unfamiliarity with internal RBAC conventions — assigned buddy.
- Promotion candidate self-note (example):
  - Objective list of deliverables in the review period with links and outcomes.
  - Two peer references and a short impact statement.

Operational considerations and best practices:
- Keep signal bandwidth low: only submit signals you would include in a promotion packet. If evidence is weak, mark as "needs more data." 
- Avoid over-reliance on single metrics; use the weighted rubric above.
- Ensure all packet artifacts are accessible to People Ops and relevant calibrators.

Change history and governance:
- This playbook is owned by People Ops. Major changes must be approved by the Head of People Ops and communicated one quarter in advance.
- Minor changes (template tweaks, rubric weight adjustments <=5%) can be applied directly by People Ops with a one-week notice to stakeholders.

Related resources:
- Promotion pathways and calibration protocol (link in related_pages).
- First year engagement milestones (link in related_pages).
- HR formal casework and investigation process (internal legal link).

Appendix: example JSON payload for a single packet (for integrators / scripts):
- Note: include to help SRE or Eng DX automate uploads; store in the team repo for automation.

Usage notes:
- Teams are encouraged to pilot a 1-month trial using the radar for a single pod before full org rollout. People Ops will provide a pilot checklist and dedicated support.

If you have questions or want the packet template as a Google form or CSV for automation, contact People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com) or ping on #people-ops.
